metadata.description: Netdust harness plugins — devops (the one branch flow, deploy gate/ledger and site.yml schema), core (business/content/ops skills), agent (the build harness: gates, hooks, reviewer agents), wp / statamic / react (stack knowledge). Stack-agnostic devops + core; the stack plugins layer on top.

plugins.name: netdust-core
plugins.description: 0.4.1: dev-stack — an env var in front of `ddev wp` never reaches the container. Netdust business + ops + content core: the per-project memory convention (STATE/lessons/todo — live hooks in netdust-agent), content/marketing skills (brand-voice, marketing, market-research), the design-builder skill (measured-motion reference recreation), the research skill, ops/infra skills (ploi, secure-server, dev-stack — DDEV/branch-flow/.env), the 9-method /deploy dispatcher, /memory-audit + /pattern-miner knowledge commands, and the ploi MCP. NOT a coding harness — the build harness (gates, craft skills, reviewer agents, TDD/threat-model/shake-out, /integration + /shakeout) lives in netdust-agent. Stack-agnostic. Layered on by netdust-wp, netdust-statamic.

plugins.name: netdust-devops
plugins.description: 0.4.0: the plugin names no caller. It acts on ONE project from inside its repo and has no opinion about what invokes it — a person, an agent, or a tool reporting across many repos; naming a caller inverted the dependency and, in a template, shipped that assumption into every scaffolded project regardless of stack. The /fleet command moved out to the fleet repo, /deploy guards on a property (site.yml + Makefile present) instead of a repo name, and a test asserts both the plugin and its SCAFFOLDED OUTPUT stay caller-free. ONE scaffolder. bin/new-project drives off templates/stacks.tsv — a (stack, template) registry where a new project shape is a ROW, not a branch of code; --template picks the skeleton (wp: bedrock|stackwp), --set overrides any token so a fleet dispatch table can drive it. Every project file now renders from templates/ (CLAUDE.md, .gitignore, memory/, tasks/ were inline heredocs); the generic CLAUDE.md finally teaches the DECISION:/RISK:/LESSON:/TODO: tag conventions the Stop hook keys on, which no non-WP project had ever been told. `make push env=<env>` (local DB → a non-production environment, refusing production by name) replaces the fleet's db-push.sh; structure.theme_flavour restored to schema 2 — netdust-wp:wp-frontend reads it. the single source of truth for Netdust devops — the branch flow, the deploy gate and ledger, and the project/fleet contract. Ships a stack-split Makefile core (Makefile.netdust + mk/wp|statamic|node|generic|ddev) that projects VENDOR rather than copy: `make devops-update` writes a checksummed .netdust-devops stamp, so `make doctor` names any project that is behind or has a managed file edited in place. Owns site.yml schema 2 — environments: is the only place a branch is bound to a server; hosting.remote_path_*, deploy.staging_command/production_command and the makefile/git-bundle-makefile/rsync-staging-prod methods are retired. One scaffolder (bin/new-project --stack=), one skill, one /deploy. Replaces the flow half of netdust-core:dev-stack and both former /deploy commands. Project layer does everything; the fleet layer (netdust-wp-manager) reads and reports only.

plugins.name: netdust-agent
plugins.description: 0.21.3: lessons — the flow-floor guard keys on quoted text, no-origin deadlock, Stop hook mid-dispatch commit, cluster-open unimplemented, cluster cap on plan corrections. 0.21.2: a lane-less tasks.md WARNs — the AC-2 silence is for legacy-waived artifacts only; planning: an older plan in the project is not the grammar. 0.21.1: the stop hook writes memory/ at the project root (walks up from a vendor-tree cwd, never writes under themes/plugins/vendor/packages). Netdust overlay on superpowers — superpowers is the process workhorse (brainstorm, plan, TDD, review, finish); netdust-agent adds the gates: an intake router (class A–F priced by open decisions + a stakes dial), plan-time gates machine-checked by bin/gate-check.py (threat model, invariants, ground-truth, Source: per FR, deliverable-first ordering, behaviour clusters), build-time gates (tier-based testing through the netdust WP harness, review clusters with independent reviewers, feature tests by an independent test-author after each task group), and a self-contained machine layer (hooks + bin/ scripts, bare python3) that verifies artifacts instead of trusting testimony. 0.18 (the re-thinning): 27 skills cut to 6 thin overlays that actually invoke their superpowers base; verify-budget is telemetry, never a HALT; skills ship with evals; and an on-demand convergence gate (/converge) — the codebase read against specs/<feature>/ for what was promised but never built, gaps appended to tasks.md as a PROPOSED phase behind gate-check + the seam.

plugins.name: netdust-wp
plugins.description: 1.1.2: lessons §6 singles built in the builder (self-echo, custom<Type> id, library starters), `yoo-content.php library` verbs, the attachment-relation gap in baseline.md + ntdst-core-gaps, a drift-reviewer calibration. 1.1.1: the deploy template carries the fixes projects had to re-apply (set -f on deploy.exclude, structure.webroot, project-named dumps, a flow-floor-aware promote test). 1.1.0: ntdst-yootheme v2 — the baseline yootheme module instead of a per-project source, yoo-lint (16 silent-trap codes against the installed parent), yoo-measure + yoo-recompile, yoo_layout.py + a section catalogue, workflow.md (the Figma → LESS → sections → assemble → measure loop), lessons by task; anchored on YOOtheme 5.0.43 with 5.0.41 as the CVE floor. Netdust WordPress plugin — WP discipline, WP planning (plan-requirements gate + golden-path slice), WP reference, ntdst-core framework + golden-path feature exemplars, WP commands. Layers on netdust-core. 1.0.0 teaches ntdst-core 5.2.0.

plugins.name: netdust-statamic
plugins.description: Netdust Statamic plugin — Statamic 6 + Peak skills, build playbook, shake-out, scaffolding commands. Layers on netdust-core.

plugins.name: netdust-react
plugins.description: Netdust React plugin — Vite + React 18 + TypeScript + Tailwind, packaged to iOS/Android with Capacitor. Skills: react-architecture (project shape, the gate wiring standards-gate/testing-workflow read, storage-durability rules — localStorage is not durable on iOS — and the web/native seam), capacitor-react (native feature access from React; vendored from capawesome-team/skills, MIT). Templates for the thin mechanical layer only: strict tsconfig, eslint with feature-boundary + persistence-convergence rules, prettier, lefthook, knip. Deliberately thin and grown from real builds rather than authored ahead of them. Layers on netdust-core and netdust-agent.
